stages.title: Start with the language
stages.goal: Learn one small concept at a time, starting with variables.
stages.checkpoint: Calculate the total study minutes for an array of lessons using a function, loop and condition.

stages.title: Work with data and scope
stages.goal: Transform collections, validate input, then understand bindings and built-in utilities.
stages.checkpoint: Explain a closure and build a validated calculation without accidental string concatenation.

stages.title: Build browser interactions
stages.goal: Learn HTML/CSS structure before manipulating the DOM.
stages.checkpoint: Build a keyboard-accessible list with delegated actions.

stages.title: Understand objects and design
stages.goal: Learn receivers and prototypes before the OOP project.
stages.checkpoint: Explain this for three call sites and implement the small state-machine project.

stages.title: Handle asynchronous work and delivery
stages.goal: Progress from promises and fetching to concurrency limits and modules.
stages.checkpoint: Handle a failed request, cap concurrent work, and explain how the app reaches the browser.

stages.title: Components before architecture
stages.goal: Start with JSX and props, add state, then understand rendering and identity.
stages.checkpoint: Build an editable list whose drafts remain attached to the correct items.

stages.title: Reuse UI and synchronize safely
stages.goal: Learn composition, then effects, refs and custom hooks.
stages.checkpoint: Extract a reusable component and clean up a cancellable effect.

stages.title: Connect a complete application
stages.goal: Add navigation, shared state, server-state caching and typed boundaries.
stages.checkpoint: Build a routed page with explicit cache identity and validated API data.

stages.title: Measure and practice
stages.goal: Profile production behavior before the machine-coding exercise.
stages.checkpoint: Demonstrate stale-request protection, keyboard behavior and one measured improvement.

stages.title: Write your first Java programs
stages.goal: Run main, declare variables, make decisions, write methods, and create instances.
stages.checkpoint: Compile a learner program with two independent objects and a method that processes an array.

stages.title: Build a reliable core model
stages.goal: Extend basic classes with OOP, collections, exceptions, streams and memory reasoning.
stages.checkpoint: Choose a collection, preserve equality contracts and close an owned resource.

stages.title: Build test and persist
stages.goal: Set up builds and tests before database access and SQL concurrency exercises.
stages.checkpoint: Test a JDBC operation and explain a join and an atomic inventory update.

stages.title: Create Spring applications
stages.goal: Move from dependency injection and REST to persistence and security.
stages.checkpoint: Implement a validated resource endpoint with a transaction and authorization boundary.

stages.title: Operate concurrent services
stages.goal: Study thread safety, resource limits and production signals after the application model.
stages.checkpoint: Demonstrate a race-safe operation and distinguish pool wait from execution time.

stages.title: Understand the server request
stages.goal: Start with Node and HTTP, then learn Express routing and errors.
stages.checkpoint: Trace a request through middleware to a controlled response.

stages.title: Store and model data
stages.goal: Learn documents and CRUD before introducing Mongoose schemas.
stages.checkpoint: Choose embedding or references for a concrete access pattern and validate writes.

stages.title: Query efficiently
stages.goal: Learn indexes and aggregation, then inspect query plans and bounded streaming.
stages.checkpoint: Explain the winning plan for a tenant-scoped query and stream a large export.

stages.title: Secure and ship
stages.goal: Add authentication and authorization before payment/upload/deployment integration.
stages.checkpoint: Reject unauthorized resource access and recover safely from a duplicate webhook.

stages.title: Understand cost and basic structures
stages.goal: Start with complexity, lists/stacks/queues, and hashing before pattern-based problems.
stages.checkpoint: Choose an array, queue or map and justify operation costs.

stages.title: Learn reusable problem-solving patterns
stages.goal: Use familiar structures for counters, pointers and search; then introduce recursion and sorting.
stages.checkpoint: State a binary-search invariant and trace a recursive call before coding.

stages.title: Handle ordered candidates and hierarchies
stages.goal: Apply stack invariants, then learn trees and heaps before graphs.
stages.checkpoint: Prove the stack bound and implement a heap-based top-k solution.

stages.title: Solve graph and dynamic-programming problems
stages.goal: Build on queues, recursion, hashing and heaps to reason about dependencies and repeated subproblems.
stages.checkpoint: Choose BFS versus Dijkstra, then derive a DP state and recurrence.

stages.title: Shared design foundations
stages.goal: Clarify requirements and capacity before choosing scaling and caching components.
stages.checkpoint: State workload, latency, freshness and correctness assumptions for a service.

stages.title: React frontend architecture
stages.goal: Design rendering, state and performance before the frontend interview case.
stages.checkpoint: Design an accessible catalog with URL state, caching and stale-request handling.

stages.title: Java backend architecture
stages.goal: Design APIs and data boundaries, then messaging, reliability and operations.
stages.checkpoint: Explain a reservation invariant, retry identity and failure recovery timeline.

stages.title: End-to-end case studies
stages.goal: Combine frontend and backend reasoning only after studying both sides.
stages.checkpoint: Walk through checkout and real-time reconnection failures without losing durable state.

stages.title: Language interview practice
stages.goal: Use the playbook for the language you have finished studying.
stages.checkpoint: Explain an output question and defend a design choice without reading the answer.

stages.title: Application interview practice
stages.goal: Move from language reasoning to frontend and data-backed application scenarios.
stages.checkpoint: Complete one machine-coding or query-design drill with error cases.

stages.title: Algorithms and architecture practice
stages.goal: Use these rounds after the corresponding DSA or design course.
stages.checkpoint: State an invariant in a coding round and a measurable requirement in a design round.
